Extend orchestrator/worker_control.py with steer(task_id, message, *, reason, source="planner") -> dict. Record first: append {ts, task, reason, message, source} to .orchestrator/workers/<task>.steering.jsonl and a registry event steer (message length only in the event, the text lives in the steering file); bus event on the task (bus.update with an events entry if the bus supports it, else reason field untouched) and packet_meta.steering_count incremented; the task's spec, acceptance and scope are never modified. Delivery: registry status steering; interrupt the running process as cancel does but with hold skipped (SIGTERM, grace, SIGKILL), then resume with the steering text prepended by 'Steering from <source> (<reason>):' and followed by 'The original task contract is unchanged.': Codex workers via executor.resume-style call on the recorded thread (see codex_reply and executor.argv_for kind resume; the worktree cwd selects the thread's worktree); Claude workers via spawn with the recorded packet_meta.session_id using claude -p --resume <session_id> (add a resume path to spawn.run_worker or a small spawn.resume_worker(task, prompt, session_id) that reuses the launch code, tools and env of the original role). When no session or thread is recorded, steer refuses with a clear error and leaves the worker running. Registry status back to running after resume with event steered. CLI: `orchestrator workers steer <task> --reason <text> --message <text>`. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md gains the steering section including the immutability rule.
Spec review T-1197 folded in: (1) Coordination with the interrupted worker's thread: the registry entry carries an integer epoch (starts at 1 on spawn); steer() increments it when it interrupts and records it on the entry; spawn and executor capture the epoch at launch and pass it to worker_registry.finish(task_id, ..., epoch=) and to their bus.post_result path, and finish() (scope adds orchestrator/worker_registry.py and tests/test_worker_registry.py) ignores a call whose epoch is older than the entry's, so the killed worker's late cleanup can never clobber the resumed run; the resumed run uses the new epoch. (2) worker_registry.FIELDS gains message_chars (int) for the steer event. (3) Codex delivery uses a dedicated executor.steer_resume(task, thread, message) that runs codex exec resume <thread> with the framed message directly (same access flags as argv_for kind resume), never executor.reply() and never resume_plan(), and does not touch the fix-loop rounds counter; a test asserts reply() is not called.
Spec review T-1210 folded in: (1) worker_registry.upsert(status='starting') carries the existing entry's epoch forward (and any explicit epoch kwarg wins), so a resumed launch that passes through the normal launch bookkeeping never resets it. (2) The epoch guard also covers capacity: executor.start's finally and spawn.run_worker release the pool reservation through worker_control.release_if_current(task_id, epoch, pool) which releases only when the epoch is still the entry's; the resumed run owns the reservation. (3) The interrupted thread's late bus writes are guarded without touching bus.py: steer() stamps pipeline.steer_epoch on the task; daemon._dispatch_worker (daemon.py joins the scope) and spawn.run_worker compare their launch epoch with pipeline.steer_epoch before bus.post_result/bus.update and skip when older. (4) Extract the SIGTERM/grace/SIGKILL loop from cancel() into worker_control._terminate(pid, *, grace_s, sleep, alive, signal_fn) used by both cancel() and steer(). (5) spawn records the effective tool allowlist of each launch (after any disclosure escalation) on the registry entry (field tools, list of names); resume_worker reuses that recorded list, not TOOLS[role].
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.

orchestrator/skill_learning.py: add candidates_from_memory(root) using memory_store.search over kinds gotcha and decision: group records by shared components (at least 3 records over at least 2 distinct dates) whose bodies contain procedural language (imperative verbs such as run, check, set, use, never, always, before, after) and produce learned-skill proposals through the existing proposal path (same shape and quarantine/testing lifecycle as today's learned skills; provenance memory with the record ids). When a proposal's skill is promoted to active, memory_store.add records a tag skill:<skill_id> on each source record and memory_hot renders such records as one line pointing at the skill instead of the full body. orchestrator/strategy.py: at merge time (new hook: daemon.py joins the scope; in the merge path that marks a task merged, call strategy.record_outcome(task, state_dir=STATE) (daemon.py already binds the name root to failures.root; never shadow it) which computes the token, usd, duration and fix-round figures the way strategy.observations() does today and writes the record) write one memory_store record kind strategy per merged execute task: title '<task_class> <band> <strategy name>', tags task_class:<x>, band:<b>, strategy:<name>, outcome first_pass|fix_rounds:<n>, body with tokens, duration, executor, fix rounds; source_task and source_goal set. CLI `orchestrator memory strategies [--task-class x] [--band b] [--json]` aggregates strategy records: per strategy name the count, first-pass rate, median tokens and duration, so the Planner asks what worked for this kind of task without reading retrospectives. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/17-memory-skills-strategy.md.
Spec review T-1182 folded in: (1) The merge-time hook is new (daemon.py never called strategy.py): implement strategy.record_outcome(task, root) reusing the computation of strategy.observations(), called from the daemon's merge path (scope adds orchestrator/daemon.py and tests/test_daemon.py). (2) Tagging source records with skill:<skill_id> lives inside skills_registry.transition() when the new state is active (scope adds orchestrator/skills_registry.py), so both `skills promote` and the generic `skills transition` paths tag. (3) Proposals from memory get roles = the union of the role fields of the source records' source tasks (looked up on the bus when present) with 'execute' as the default, never an empty list; a test asserts a proposal is selectable for execute. (4) Record shape for strategy records: Record.outcome holds first_pass or fix_rounds:<n>; tags carry only task_class:<x>, band:<b>, strategy:<name>; `memory strategies` aggregates on those fields.
Spec review T-1192 folded in: (1) root conventions are explicit: memory_store and memory_hot take the REPO root (Path(root)/'.orchestrator'/...), strategy, skill_learning and skills_registry take the .orchestrator STATE directory; when one calls the other, convert (state_dir.parent for the repo root) and say so in a comment; the tests follow each module's harness convention. (2) The merge hook resolves the lineage root first (attribution.lineage / strategy._root_id) so a fix-round merge records the outcome for the root task; one record per merged lineage root. (3) Strategy record id is deterministic and unique per task: id = 'strategy-<task_id>' passed explicitly to memory_store.add, never derived from kind/date/title. (4) Roles for memory-sourced proposals: read the source tasks' JSON from state_dir/tasks/<id>.json the way skill_learning._tasks does, never bus.get; missing files count as no role; default ['execute']. (5) Confidence for memory-sourced patterns: min(1.0, records/5) multiplied by min(1.0, distinct_dates/3), evidence_strength = record count; the existing propose() threshold (0.6) applies unchanged, so a group needs at least 3 records over at least 2 dates and typically 3 dates to pass; document the formula in 17-memory-skills-strategy.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Task worktrees carry no .orchestrator runs, tasks or decision_log state: tests use synthetic fixtures; for any measured numbers in docs run read-only against /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator via an explicit root argument. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Contracts of the earlier modules: .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and docs/hermes-hardening/*.md on this branch; read the merged modules before building on them.

import _harness

import json
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from orchestrator import skill_discovery, skill_learning, skills_registry


class SkillLearningTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name) / ".orchestrator"
        (self.root / "tasks").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.root / "runs/jev").mkdir(parents=True)

    def seed(self, count=5, failures=1):
        gate = []
        for index in range(count):
            task = f"T-{index}"
            accepted = index < count - failures
            (self.root / f"tasks/{task}.json").write_text(json.dumps({
                "id": task, "role": "execute", "title": "Repair parser safely",
                "spec": "Inspect the parser implementation and run the focused verification before finishing.",
                "merged_into": "main" if accepted else None, "task_class": "feature"}))
            gate.extend([{"task": task, "role": "execute", "tool": "Read", "tool_target": "src/parser.py", "ts": index},
                         {"task": task, "role": "execute", "tool": "Bash", "tool_target": "uv run unittest", "ts": index + .1}])
        (self.root / "runs/jev/gate.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(row) + "\n" for row in gate))

    def test_repeated_successful_sequence_becomes_pattern_with_support_and_counterexamples(self):
        self.seed()
        found = [p for p in skill_learning.patterns(self.root) if p["source"] == "tool_sequence"]
        self.assertEqual(1, len(found))
        self.assertEqual(5, found[0]["support"])
        self.assertEqual(4, found[0]["successes"])
        self.assertEqual(["T-4"], found[0]["failures"])
        self.assertEqual(.8, found[0]["confidence"])
        self.assertEqual(.5, found[0]["evidence_strength"])

    def test_one_off_behaviour_never_qualifies(self):
        self.seed(1, 0)
        self.assertEqual([], skill_learning.patterns(self.root))

    def test_propose_writes_quarantined_draft_never_active(self):
        self.seed()
        record = skill_learning.propose(skill_learning.patterns(self.root)[0], self.root)
        self.assertTrue(Path(record["source"]).is_relative_to(self.root / "skills/quarantine/learned"))
        self.assertEqual("quarantined", record["state"])
        state = skills_registry.state(record["id"], self.root)
        self.assertEqual("quarantined", state["state"])
        self.assertEqual("learned proposal", state["history"][-1]["reason"])
        self.assertEqual([], skills_registry.candidates({"title": "Repair parser safely"}, "execute", root=self.root))

    def test_reproposal_updates_version_not_duplicate(self):
        self.seed()
        pattern = skill_learning.patterns(self.root)[0]
        first = skill_learning.propose(pattern, self.root)
        pattern["successes"] = 5
        second = skill_learning.propose(pattern, self.root)
        records = json.loads((self.root / "skills/discovered.json").read_text())["skills"]
        self.assertEqual(1, len(records))
        self.assertEqual(first["id"], second["id"])
        self.assertNotEqual(first["version"], second["version"])
        self.assertIn("version", skills_registry.state(first["id"], self.root)["history"][-1]["reason"])

    def test_low_confidence_refused_with_reason(self):
        value = skill_learning.propose({"procedure_signature": "x", "support": 3,
                                        "support_tasks": ["a", "b", "c"], "confidence": .5}, self.root)
        self.assertTrue(value["refused"])
        self.assertIn("confidence", value["reason"])

    def test_learned_records_coexist_with_external_records_in_store(self):
        self.seed()
        external = {"skills": {"external/x/y": {"id": "external/x/y", "provenance": "external",
                    "provenance_info": {"source_repo": "x", "source_path": "y/SKILL.md"}}}}
        path = self.root / "skills/discovered.json"; path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(external))
        learned = skill_learning.propose(skill_learning.patterns(self.root)[0], self.root)
        records = json.loads(path.read_text())["skills"]
        self.assertIn("external/x/y", records)
        self.assertIn(learned["id"], records)
        candidate = ("x", "z/SKILL.md", None, "external", {"SKILL.md": b"# Z\n"}, None, "x", None, [])
        skill_discovery._store(candidate, self.root)

    def test_cli_learn_lists_and_proposes(self):
        self.seed()
        env = {**os.environ, "ORCH_ROOT": str(Path(self.temp.name))}
        listed = subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "orchestrator", "skills", "learn"], cwd=_harness.REPO,
                                env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(0, listed.returncode, listed.stderr)
        self.assertIn("tool_sequence", listed.stdout)
        proposed = subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "orchestrator", "skills", "learn", "--propose"], cwd=_harness.REPO,
                                  env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(0, proposed.returncode, proposed.stderr)
        self.assertIn("learned/", proposed.stdout)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import json
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import _harness  # noqa: F401 - share the suite's single isolated ORCH_ROOT
from orchestrator import strategy


class StrategyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name) / "repo" / ".orchestrator"
        (self.root / "tasks").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.root / "runs").mkdir()

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def write(self, task):
        (self.root / "tasks" / f'{task["id"]}.json').write_text(json.dumps(task))

    def test_derive_attributes_strategy_steps_and_components(self):
        root = {"id": "T-root", "role": "execute", "parent": "G", "created_at": 2,
                "pipeline": {"review_reason": "diff_unavailable"}}
        rows = [root,
                {"id": "T-s", "role": "scout", "parent": "G", "created_at": 1,
                 "constraints": {"objective": "dependency-map"}},
                {"id": "T-spec", "role": "spec_review", "inputs": ["T-root"]},
                {"id": "T-a", "role": "review", "inputs": ["T-root"],
                 "constraints": {"reviewer_role": "acceptance"}},
                {"id": "T-b", "role": "review", "inputs": ["T-root"],
                 "constraints": {"reviewer_role": "adversarial"}},
                {"id": "T-fix", "role": "execute", "constraints": {"fix_round_for": "T-root"}}]
        got = strategy.derive(root, {row["id"]: row for row in rows}, [{"wave": ["T-root", "T-x"]}])
        self.assertEqual(got["strategy"], "dependency_scout_execute+execute_specialist_review+security_context_strong_execute_security_review+parallel_wave")
        self.assertEqual(got["steps"], ["scout", "spec_review", "execute", "review", "security_review", "fix_round"])
        self.assertEqual(got["components"], got["strategy"].split("+"))

    def test_observations_use_real_bus_fields_and_lineage_sums(self):
        self.write({"id": "T-root", "role": "execute", "parent": "G", "complexity": 5,
                    "constraints": {"task_class": "unfamiliar"}, "executor": "codex", "created_at": 10,
                    "merged_into": "goal/G", "pipeline": {"merged_at": 25}})
        self.write({"id": "T-fix", "role": "execute", "constraints": {"fix_round_for": "T-root"},
                    "pipeline": {"gate_reds": 1}})
        self.write({"id": "T-r", "role": "review", "inputs": ["T-fix"], "tier": "strong",
                    "result": {"verdict": "request_changes"}})
        metrics = {"tasks": {"T-root": {"usd": 2, "tokens": 30, "fix_rounds": 1,
                                          "first_pass": False, "goal_id": "G"}}}
        with patch.object(strategy.scorecard_api, "efficiency", return_value=metrics):
            row, = strategy.observations(self.root)
        self.assertTrue(row["accepted"])
        self.assertEqual((row["time_s"], row["gate_reds"], row["review_request_changes"]), (15, 1, 1))
        self.assertEqual((row["task_class"], row["band"]), ("unfamiliar", "4-6"))

    def test_observations_aggregate_outcomes_per_strategy(self):
        rows = [{"strategy": "direct_execute", "task_class": "unfamiliar", "band": "4-6", "accepted": True,
                 "first_pass": True, "usd": 1, "time_s": 3, "fix_rounds": 0},
                {"strategy": "direct_execute", "task_class": "unfamiliar", "band": "4-6", "accepted": False,
                 "first_pass": False, "usd": 3, "time_s": None, "fix_rounds": 1},
                {"strategy": "scout_execute", "task_class": "unfamiliar", "band": "4-6", "accepted": True,
                 "first_pass": False, "usd": 2, "time_s": 4, "fix_rounds": 1}]
        with patch.object(strategy, "observations", return_value=rows):
            card = strategy.scorecard(self.root)
        self.assertEqual(card[("direct_execute", "unfamiliar", "4-6")]["n"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(card[("direct_execute", "unfamiliar", "4-6")]["accepted_rate"], .5)
        self.assertEqual(card[("direct_execute", "unfamiliar", "4-6")]["first_pass_rate"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(card[("direct_execute", "unfamiliar", "4-6")]["median_usd"], 2)

    def test_first_pass_rate_ignores_unknown_values(self):
        rows = [{"strategy": "direct_execute", "task_class": "unfamiliar", "band": "4-6",
                 "accepted": True, "first_pass": value, "usd": 1, "time_s": 1, "fix_rounds": 0}
                for value in (None, True, False)]
        with patch.object(strategy, "observations", return_value=rows):
            row = strategy.scorecard(self.root)[("direct_execute", "unfamiliar", "4-6")]
        self.assertEqual(row["first_pass_rate"], .5)
        self.assertEqual(row["first_pass_defined_count"], 2)

    def test_cold_start_and_insufficient_evidence_return_no_strategy(self):
        with patch.object(strategy, "observations", return_value=[]):
            cold = strategy.recommend("unfamiliar", "4-6", root=self.root)
        with patch.object(strategy, "observations", return_value=[self.sample("direct_execute", True)]):
            small = strategy.recommend("unfamiliar", "4-6", root=self.root)
        self.assertEqual((cold["strategy"], small["strategy"]), (None, None))
        self.assertEqual(cold["reason"], "insufficient_evidence")
        self.assertTrue(cold["required"])

    def sample(self, name, accepted, repo="repo", task_class="unfamiliar"):
        return {"strategy": name, "task_class": task_class, "band": "4-6", "repo": repo,
                "accepted": accepted, "first_pass": accepted, "usd": 1 if accepted else 2}

    def test_shadow_recommendation_prefers_evidence_without_changing_policy(self):
        rows = ([self.sample("direct_execute", i < 8) for i in range(12)]
                + [self.sample("scout_execute", i < 11) for i in range(12)])
        with patch.object(strategy, "observations", return_value=rows):
            shadow = strategy.recommend("unfamiliar", "4-6", repo="repo", root=self.root)
            off = strategy.recommend("unfamiliar", "4-6", repo="repo", root=self.root,
                                     cfg={"strategy": {"mode": "off"}})
        self.assertEqual((shadow["mode"], shadow["strategy"]), ("shadow", "scout_execute"))
        self.assertIsNone(off["strategy"])

    def test_repository_and_task_class_are_separated(self):
        rows = ([self.sample("direct_execute", True) for _ in range(10)]
                + [self.sample("scout_execute", True, repo="elsewhere") for _ in range(12)]
                + [self.sample("parallel_wave", True, task_class="security") for _ in range(12)])
        with patch.object(strategy, "observations", return_value=rows):
            got = strategy.recommend("unfamiliar", "4-6", repo="repo", root=self.root)
        self.assertEqual(got["strategy"], "direct_execute")
        self.assertNotIn("scout_execute", got["evidence"])
        self.assertNotIn("parallel_wave", got["evidence"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

diff --git a/docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md b/docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md
index 9915f9f..b9af7cf 100644
--- a/docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md
+++ b/docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md
@@ -51,3 +51,42 @@ reconciliation checks the current registry, even when its bus snapshot is older,
 and returns `cancelled` without bus updates for cancelling or cancelled entries.
 The Planner owns any subsequent re-specification. This is an explicit control
 operation; it introduces no adaptive routing or automatic cancellation policy.
+
+
+## Steering
+
+`orchestrator workers steer T-0001 --reason "New evidence" --message "Inspect the failing check"`
+interrupts and resumes a recorded conversation. The call waits for the resumed
+worker's result, using the normal role timeout. This explicit Planner control
+introduces no adaptive policy or shadow-mode changes to worker prompts.
+
+`worker_control.steer(task_id, message, reason=..., source="planner")` first
+appends a durable row with ts, task, reason, message, and source to
+`.orchestrator/workers/<task>.steering.jsonl`. Text is credential-redacted before
+persistence and delivery. The registry's `steer` event contains only the message
+character count and runtime metadata. The bus update records an event and
+increments `packet_meta.steering_count`; the existing reason field is preserved.
+The original spec, acceptance criteria, and scope are immutable: steering never
+rewrites any part of that task contract.
+
+The registry enters `steering`, advances its integer epoch (initially 1), and
+stamps `pipeline.steer_epoch` before interrupting the PID. The same bounded
+SIGTERM/grace/SIGKILL routine as cancellation runs, without holding the task or
+releasing its reservation. Missing thread/session identifiers refuse before any
+signal or steering write. Unsafe PIDs also refuse. Signal failures leave the
+recorded steering state and reservation available for operator recovery.
+
+Delivery is framed as `Steering from <source> (<reason>):`, the message, then
+`The original task contract is unchanged.` Codex uses a dedicated
+`executor.steer_resume` with `codex exec resume <thread>` and the resume access
+flags; process cwd selects the worktree. It never calls reply or resume_plan
+and never increments the fix-loop rounds counter. Claude uses
+`claude -p --resume <session_id>` through the original role launch path, reusing
+the recorded account, model, and effective tool allowlist, including any prior
+disclosure escalation. Environment policy and read-only role restrictions apply.
+
+The resumed process records `steered` and returns to `running` at launch;
+normal completion then records its terminal status. Launch bookkeeping preserves
+the advanced epoch. Old finish calls, late bus result/status writes, and capacity
+releases are guarded by their captured launch epoch. The resumed run owns the
+existing reservation and releases it when it finishes.

+# Memory, skills, and workflow strategy
+
+Recurring procedural gotchas and decisions can seed learned-skill proposals. Records are grouped by shared component when at least three records span at least two distinct dates and contain procedural language. Candidate confidence is `min(1, records / 5) * min(1, distinct dates / 3)` and evidence strength is the record count. The normal 0.6 proposal threshold, quarantine, testing, shadow, and activation lifecycle remains in force.
+
+Memory-sourced proposals preserve their source record IDs. Their roles are the union of roles in source task files, defaulting to `execute` when those files provide none. Activating the skill adds a `skill:<skill id>` tag to every source record; the generated HOT view then points at the learned skill instead of repeating the procedural body.
+
+Every successfully merged execute lineage writes one WARM strategy record. Fix rounds resolve to their lineage root, and the deterministic ID `strategy-<root task id>` prevents duplicate records. The record outcome is either `first_pass` or `fix_rounds:<count>`; tags contain only task class, complexity band, and strategy name. Its body records tokens, cost, duration, executor, and fix rounds.
+
+Use `orchestrator memory strategies` to aggregate count, first-pass rate, median tokens, and median duration by strategy. Optional `--task-class` and `--band` filters let the Planner query comparable work, and `--json` emits structured output.

diff --git a/tests/test_context_router.py b/tests/test_context_router.py

--- a/tests/test_context_router.py
+++ b/tests/test_context_router.py
@@ -13,6 +13,38 @@ def ev(kind, location, content, task=None, commit=""):
 
 
 class ContextRouterTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_stale_source_preserves_scope_and_security_precedence(self):
+        item = ev("source_chunk", "orchestrator/auth.py:1-4", "code", commit="old")
+        for role, scope, cfg, expected in (
+                ("execute", ["orchestrator/auth.py"], {}, ("FULL", "in_scope_file")),
+                ("scout", ["orchestrator/auth.py"], {}, ("FULL", "in_scope_file")),
+                ("security_review", [], {"review": {"security_paths": ["orchestrator/*.py"]}},
+                 ("FULL", "security_path")),
+                ("execute", [], {}, ("HIDE", "stale"))):
+            with self.subTest(role=role, scope=scope):
+                routed = context_router.route({"id": "T", "scope": scope}, [item],
+                                              role=role, cfg=cfg, head_sha="new").items[0]
+                self.assertEqual((routed.level, routed.reason), expected)
+
+    def test_stale_test_result_preserves_failure_precedence(self):
+        for role, content, expected in (("review", "OK", "FULL"),
+                                        ("execute", "FAIL test_example", "FULL"),
+                                        ("execute", "OK", "HIDE")):
+            with self.subTest(role=role, content=content):
+                item = ev("test_result", "test_example", content, commit="old")
+                routed = context_router.route({"id": "T"}, [item], role=role,
+                                              head_sha="new").items[0]
+                self.assertEqual(routed.level, expected)
+
+    def test_worker_partial_fresh_overlap_never_hidden_and_stale_hidden(self):
+        item = evidence.make("worker_partial", "T-old:abc", "file: router.py", commit="abc",
+                             provenance="worker_partial", scope=["router.py"])
+        task = {"id": "T-new", "scope": [], "packet_read_scope": ["router.py"]}
+        fresh = context_router.route(task, [item], role="execute", head_sha="abc").items[0]
+        stale = context_router.route(task, [item], role="execute", head_sha="def").items[0]
+        self.assertEqual((fresh.level, fresh.reason), ("LONG", "prior_worker_overlap"))
+        self.assertEqual((stale.level, stale.reason), ("HIDE", "stale"))
+
     def test_security_review_full_for_security_path_in_scope(self):

Verify with the git log that the change sits on top of the goal head, then run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until it exits 0. Do not change behaviour beyond conflict resolution; do not ask questions; report the resolved files and failures-only output.
Original task spec for reference (already implemented in the cherry-picked commits):
orchestrator/evidence.py: add provenance value worker_partial to PROVENANCE (trust_class LOCAL_USER, trust field untrusted stays as for non-repo provenance, scan applied as for any evidence). orchestrator/worker_control.py: after cancel builds the partial result, and in a new hook worker_control.preserve_partial(task) that daemon.reconcile_dead calls for a dead worker with a dirty worktree, create evidence objects in the goal's evidence pool (evidence.make with source_type worker_partial, location the task id plus the worktree head sha, content = the partial facts rendered as compact lines: files changed with diff stat, commits with subjects, tests run and their result lines, error tail, files inspected; commit = worktree head sha; freshness by the existing hash mechanism). Replacement routing: orchestrator/context_router.py treats worker_partial evidence whose location task shares the same goal and overlaps the current task's scope (write or read) as high relevance (never HIDE) with a cap of [context_router].partial_max_tokens (default 800, dated comment); orchestrator/spawn.py renders those items under a packet section prior_worker (after evidence) with the source task id and the head sha, so the new worker can check out or diff it instead of rediscovering; the section is empty when nothing applies. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/16-evidence-reuse.md.
Spec review T-1198 folded in: (1) evidence.py: add worker_partial to BOTH SOURCE_TYPES and PROVENANCE (make() validates each separately) and add an explicit entry worker_partial -> LOCAL_USER in the _trust_class dict, documenting in the module docstring that LOCAL_USER covers locally produced artifacts (memory and observed worker outputs), not only user-authored memory. (2) fresh() and context_router's duplicate/staleness check are extended so worker_partial evidence goes stale when its commit differs from the goal head (same commit == head_sha rule as source_chunk and test_result). (3) Shadow-first: the prior_worker section is rendered only when [context_router].mode is active; in shadow the would-be section (ids and chars) is logged on the context_route decision row and the packet is unchanged. (4) preserve_partial is idempotent: it stamps pipeline.partial_preserved_at on the task and returns early when the stamp exists, so reconcile_dead re-runs every tick without growing the pool. (5) Overlap is computed from persisted data only: the dead task's write scope against the current task's write scope plus its packet-time read scope; no read footprint of the dead task is stored. (6) tests/test_worker_control.py exists with class WorkerControl; add the new test as a method there.
Spec review T-1211 folded in: (1) The evidence object gains an optional field scope (list of paths, default empty, persisted and backfilled like trust_class); preserve_partial fills it with the dead task's write scope, so context_router.relevance_for computes worker_partial overlap from ev.scope against the current task's write scope plus packet-time read scope; the location stays task_id:head_sha and bus.py is untouched. (2) Precedence: staleness wins; a worker_partial item whose commit is not the goal head is HIDE (stale), and only a fresh overlapping item is 'never HIDE'. (3) The cap is enforced at creation time: preserve_partial truncates the rendered content to [context_router].partial_max_tokens times 4 chars (mirroring worker_control._bounded_result), so the router needs no per-item cap. (4) SOURCE_TYPES, PROVENANCE and the _trust_class entry change together in one commit with one test that make(source_type=worker_partial, provenance=worker_partial) succeeds and yields LOCAL_USER.

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+# Stable prompt prefixes
+
+On 2026-09-23, the execute, review, scout, and spec-review role rules moved ahead of the packet boundary. Wording and rule order did not change. The packet body remains task-specific, so rearranging sections within it cannot lengthen the prefix measured before its header.
+
+## Fixture measurement
+
+The measurement uses `spawn.render` with the shared synthetic widget task from `tests/test_spawn.py`. Before the move, every template began at the packet boundary and therefore had a zero-character prefix. After the move:
+
+| Role | Before | After |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| execute | 0 | 1,574 |
+| review | 0 | 710 |
+| scout | 0 | 648 |
+| spec-review | 0 | 686 |
+
+These are the off-mode results and cover template text only. With active conditional instruction composition on the same fixture, execute measures 725 characters while review, scout, and spec-review remain 710, 648, and 686. The active values can change with module selection as described below.
+
+## Remaining launch differences
+
+| Prefix input | Per-role or per-run difference | Cache impact | Disposition |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| MCP configuration | A role-specific `.mcp.<role>.json` is used when present; otherwise workers share `.mcp.worker.json`. | Different disclosed MCP schemas prevent cross-role reuse. | Unavoidable when a role needs a distinct server set; the shared fallback is retained elsewhere. |
+| Allowed tools | `spawn.py` supplies a different `--allowedTools` list for execute, review, scout, and spec-review. | Tool definitions differ by role and split prefixes. | Unavoidable least-privilege boundary. |
+| Disallowed tools | Non-execute roles add Edit, Write, and NotebookEdit to `--disallowedTools`; execute does not. | The launch instruction surface differs from execute. | Unavoidable enforcement of read-only roles. |
+| Conditional instruction modules | In active mode, selected rule modules are composed according to task and role signals. Shadow mode preserves the legacy prompt. | Different selected modules create multiple prefixes within a role. | Intentional and avoidable only by disabling active conditional loading; telemetry must expose the tradeoff. |
+| Tool disclosure levels | Active disclosure can reduce the role allowlist according to selected skills; off and shadow retain the static role list. Skill presentation can also vary by selection level. | Different tool schemas or disclosed skill text create multiple prefixes within a role. | Intentional adaptive behavior; shadow is byte-identical and only records decisions. |
+
+`scorecard --cache` now prints a focused per-role table with the existing `distinct_prefix_sha`, `runs`, and `reuse_rate` values. No run-row field or bus schema changed. Over time, repeated runs with the same role prefix raise `reuse_rate`; unavoidable role boundaries remain visible as separate rows.

diff --git a/docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md b/docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md
index 9915f9f..ca58bdf 100644
--- a/docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md
+++ b/docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md
@@ -51,3 +51,51 @@ reconciliation checks the current registry, even when its bus snapshot is older,
 and returns `cancelled` without bus updates for cancelling or cancelled entries.
 The Planner owns any subsequent re-specification. This is an explicit control
 operation; it introduces no adaptive routing or automatic cancellation policy.
+
+
+## Steering
+
+`orchestrator workers steer T-0001 --reason "New evidence" --message "Inspect the failing check"`
+interrupts and resumes a recorded conversation. The call waits for the resumed
+worker's result, using the normal role timeout. This explicit Planner control
+introduces no adaptive policy or shadow-mode changes to worker prompts.
+
+`worker_control.steer(task_id, message, reason=..., source="planner")` first
+appends a durable row with ts, task, reason, message, and source to
+`.orchestrator/workers/<task>.steering.jsonl`. Text is credential-redacted before
+persistence and delivery. The registry's `steer` event contains only the message
+character count and runtime metadata. The bus update records an event and
+increments `packet_meta.steering_count`; the existing reason field is preserved.
+The original spec, acceptance criteria, and scope are immutable: steering never
+rewrites any part of that task contract.
+
+The registry enters `steering`, advances its integer epoch (initially 1), and
+stamps `pipeline.steer_epoch` before interrupting the PID. The same bounded
+SIGTERM/grace/SIGKILL routine as cancellation runs, without holding the task or
+releasing its reservation. Missing thread/session identifiers refuse before any
+signal or steering write. Missing, dead, and unsafe PIDs also refuse before the
+epoch changes; a worker must have a recorded live process. Signal failures leave the
+recorded steering state and reservation available for operator recovery.
+
+Delivery is framed as `Steering from <source> (<reason>):`, the message, then
+`The original task contract is unchanged.` Codex uses a dedicated
+`executor.steer_resume` with `codex exec resume <thread>` and the resume access
+flags; process cwd selects the worktree. It never calls reply or resume_plan
+and never increments the fix-loop rounds counter. Claude uses
+`claude -p --resume <session_id>` through the original role launch path, reusing
+the recorded account, model, and effective tool allowlist, including any prior
+disclosure escalation. Environment policy and read-only role restrictions apply.
+
+The resumed process records `steered` and returns to `running` at launch;
+normal completion then records its terminal status. Launch bookkeeping preserves
+the advanced epoch. Old finish calls, late bus result/status writes, and capacity
+releases are guarded by their captured launch epoch. The resumed run owns the
+existing reservation and releases it when it finishes.
+
+
+If resume delivery raises, the current epoch records a terminal `failed` registry
+state with reason `steer_failed`. The bus returns to its pre-steering status with
+pid cleared and a redacted `pipeline.steer_failed` diagnostic. The reservation is
+released through `release_if_current`, then the original exception is re-raised.
+A newer steering epoch is never overwritten by this recovery. The durable message
+and steering counters remain available for diagnosis.

Original task spec for reference (already implemented in the cherry-picked commits):
Extend orchestrator/worker_control.py with steer(task_id, message, *, reason, source="planner") -> dict. Record first: append {ts, task, reason, message, source} to .orchestrator/workers/<task>.steering.jsonl and a registry event steer (message length only in the event, the text lives in the steering file); bus event on the task (bus.update with an events entry if the bus supports it, else reason field untouched) and packet_meta.steering_count incremented; the task's spec, acceptance and scope are never modified. Delivery: registry status steering; interrupt the running process as cancel does but with hold skipped (SIGTERM, grace, SIGKILL), then resume with the steering text prepended by 'Steering from <source> (<reason>):' and followed by 'The original task contract is unchanged.': Codex workers via executor.resume-style call on the recorded thread (see codex_reply and executor.argv_for kind resume; the worktree cwd selects the thread's worktree); Claude workers via spawn with the recorded packet_meta.session_id using claude -p --resume <session_id> (add a resume path to spawn.run_worker or a small spawn.resume_worker(task, prompt, session_id) that reuses the launch code, tools and env of the original role). When no session or thread is recorded, steer refuses with a clear error and leaves the worker running. Registry status back to running after resume with event steered. CLI: `orchestrator workers steer <task> --reason <text> --message <text>`. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/11-worker-control.md gains the steering section including the immutability rule.
Spec review T-1197 folded in: (1) Coordination with the interrupted worker's thread: the registry entry carries an integer epoch (starts at 1 on spawn); steer() increments it when it interrupts and records it on the entry; spawn and executor capture the epoch at launch and pass it to worker_registry.finish(task_id, ..., epoch=) and to their bus.post_result path, and finish() (scope adds orchestrator/worker_registry.py and tests/test_worker_registry.py) ignores a call whose epoch is older than the entry's, so the killed worker's late cleanup can never clobber the resumed run; the resumed run uses the new epoch. (2) worker_registry.FIELDS gains message_chars (int) for the steer event. (3) Codex delivery uses a dedicated executor.steer_resume(task, thread, message) that runs codex exec resume <thread> with the framed message directly (same access flags as argv_for kind resume), never executor.reply() and never resume_plan(), and does not touch the fix-loop rounds counter; a test asserts reply() is not called.
Spec review T-1210 folded in: (1) worker_registry.upsert(status='starting') carries the existing entry's epoch forward (and any explicit epoch kwarg wins), so a resumed launch that passes through the normal launch bookkeeping never resets it. (2) The epoch guard also covers capacity: executor.start's finally and spawn.run_worker release the pool reservation through worker_control.release_if_current(task_id, epoch, pool) which releases only when the epoch is still the entry's; the resumed run owns the reservation. (3) The interrupted thread's late bus writes are guarded without touching bus.py: steer() stamps pipeline.steer_epoch on the task; daemon._dispatch_worker (daemon.py joins the scope) and spawn.run_worker compare their launch epoch with pipeline.steer_epoch before bus.post_result/bus.update and skip when older. (4) Extract the SIGTERM/grace/SIGKILL loop from cancel() into worker_control._terminate(pid, *, grace_s, sleep, alive, signal_fn) used by both cancel() and steer(). (5) spawn records the effective tool allowlist of each launch (after any disclosure escalation) on the registry entry (field tools, list of names); resume_worker reuses that recorded list, not TOOLS[role].
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. content:
orchestrator/context_router.py: for every routed evidence item compute cacheability (stable for repo files at a pinned commit, semi for memory, dynamic for tool outputs, test results and worker_partial) and cache_cost = cache_telemetry.dynamic_cost(chars, provider, cfg), a new small read-only helper in orchestrator/cache_telemetry.py (scope) that applies the [cache] ratios of effective_cost to a char count (chars/4 tokens) and returns None when the [cache] section or telemetry ratios are missing. Shadow algorithm for cache_adjusted_level, defined exactly: start from the presented level; downgrade one step (FULL to LONG, LONG to SHORT) when cacheability is dynamic and cache_cost exceeds [context_router].cache_downgrade_tokens (default 600); upgrade one step (SHORT to LONG) when cacheability is stable and cache_cost is below [context_router].cache_upgrade_tokens (default 200); never change an item whose level came from a hard-constraint FULL reason (in_scope_file, security_path, failing_output, acceptance); HIDE items stay HIDE. Rows: the existing kind context_selection keeps its candidates shape; the deterministic dict gains three parallel maps keyed by evidence id: cacheability, cache_cost, cache_adjusted_level, plus cache_data = ok|missing. Presented levels never change unless [context_router].cache_mode is active (add cache_mode = "shadow" with a dated comment and revert instruction to [context_router]; missing key means off; unknown values raise at config load in pool validation; cache_mode is inert whenever the section's mode is off; tests/test_pool.py covers the validation and the gating). Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/10-cache-aware-disclosure.md section 1 with the algorithm and a reproducible command (`orchestrator scorecard --context --cache-shadow`, added to the context scorecard output, scope orchestrator/cli.py) that prints, over the decision_log rows present, the row count, date range and the share of items whose cache_adjusted_level differs from the presented level; when no rows exist the doc says so.
Spec review T-1246 folded in: (1) Validation lives in context_router.cache_mode(cfg) (returns off|shadow|active, raises ValueError on anything else; missing key is off); pool.py and tests/test_pool.py leave the scope; the validation test lives in tests/test_context_router.py. (2) Authoritative mode: spawn._context_mode's effective mode (which already downgrades active to shadow when the context eval is missing or stale) is passed into route(..., effective_mode=) by spawn.py (scope adds orchestrator/spawn.py and tests/test_spawn.py); cache_mode active applies adjusted levels only when effective_mode is active. (3) Cacheability table, explicit: stable = source_chunk, architecture_note, decision, memory_entry whose commit equals the head_sha given to route() ('pinned'); semi = scout_finding, graph_finding, review_finding, previous_result, external_doc, and any stable type whose commit differs from head_sha; dynamic = test_result and any item whose provenance is worker_partial. (4) cache_cost input: the chars of _text(ev, presented_level) (the tokens_at_level quantity), provider passed as route(..., provider=) by spawn (codex for a Codex dispatch, claude otherwise); provider None yields cache_cost None and cache_data missing. (5) Algorithm corrected: no FULL-to-LONG step (FULL only comes from hard constraints); downgrade LONG-to-SHORT only for dynamic items whose reason is not in the exempt set {hard-constraint FULL reasons, skill_required_context, read_scope, section_items}; upgrade SHORT-to-LONG only for stable items whose reason is the generic source_type fallback. (6) Plumbing: the Routed dataclass gains optional fields cacheability, cache_cost, cache_adjusted_level (default None) and RoutedPacket exposes them; decision_row writes the three parallel maps into the deterministic dict; the candidates list keeps its exact shape in shadow (a test asserts byte-identical candidates with and without cache_mode); in active mode the presented level itself changes so the candidates suffixes follow, and tokens_at_level is computed from the adjusted level.
Spec review T-1251 folded in (these rules override earlier wording where they differ): (a) There is NO upgrade rule; the only adjustment is a one-step downgrade LONG-to-SHORT. (b) cache_cost = (chars of _text(ev, presented_level) / 4) * (1 + write_ratio[provider]) with write_ratio from cache_telemetry._cache_cfg (config values merged with DEFAULT_RATIOS; defaults are fine and the row records cache_data = defaults|config); cache_cost is None and cache_data = missing only when provider is None. The downgrade threshold [context_router].cache_downgrade_tokens (default 600) compares against that cache_cost. (c) Validation: context_router.cache_mode(cfg) is called once by spawn._context_mode; an invalid value falls back to off and sets invalid_config = true on the row (mirroring promotion.current_mode); route() never raises for configuration. (d) Cacheability order, first match wins: provenance worker_partial -> dynamic; source_type test_result -> dynamic; source_type source_chunk with a non-empty commit equal to a non-None head_sha -> stable; everything else -> semi (so stable is in practice pinned source chunks; memory, decision and architecture items are semi). (e) Downgrade eligibility: only items whose reason is a generic fallback reason (the reason strings _choice assigns when no named rule matched) are eligible; every named-rule reason is exempt, including in_scope_file, security_path, failing_output, acceptance, skill_required_context, read_scope, section_items, prior_worker_overlap, unrelated, ambiguous and dependency; the docs list the eligible reason strings verbatim from _choice, and a test asserts prior_worker_overlap and skill_required_context items are untouched in active mode.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.

reserve_for_planner = 0.0
daily_budget_tokens=[REDACTED]  # 2026-09-18: was 8M; see window_cap_tokens note

[daemon]
autostart = true   # the orchestrator MCP server starts the pipeline loop in a background thread; ORCH_DAEMON=0 overrides
interval_s = 30
respawn_after_s = 120  # wait before retrying an unclaimed review or spec_review worker spawn
respawn_max = 3  # hold a review after this many respawns without a claim
stage_lease_s = 900  # retry a claimed-but-unfinished pipeline side effect after this lease expires
auto_fix_rounds = 2
close_retry_s = 900  # minimum delay between failed automatic PR attempts
close_max_attempts = 3  # then escalate close_failed; never charge gave_up
flaky_rerun_max = 1  # Default 1; rerun a held gate's named failures at most this many times to classify flakiness.
flaky_rerun_timeout_s = 600  # Default 600s; bound each held-test rerun so a hung test cannot block a daemon tick.

[planner]
autonomous = false  # 2026-09-23 17:25: off while the interactive Planner runs without an MCP host (the attached-session check cannot see it): headless launches re-filed S2a1 as a duplicate v2 (T-1078) and burned account A; revert path: autonomous = true
                     # interactive session running -- off by default (interactive Planner is a human's proxy);
                     # turn on only in the executor container, where no human session ever attaches
# Context at which the interactive Planner should hand over; decision packets are sized separately for each run.
handover_context_tokens=[REDACTED]
decision_packet_chars = 6000

[planner.routes]
# Default true; enabled = false restores the previous behaviour: every point escalates.
enabled = true
auto_open_pr = false  # Default false; close posts PR pending for the Planner instead of opening it automatically.
# Default fable; the caller resolves this alias through [models].planner, not a model ID here.
escalate_tier = "fable"
# Default sonnet; tier used to investigate small goals without review triggers.
investigate_tier = "sonnet"
# Default 4; inclusive complexity ceiling for the investigate route.
investigate_max_complexity = 4
# Default 2; exceeding this records a justified exception, never blocks a launch.
premium_launches_soft_per_goal = 2

[planner.routing]
mode = "active"  # 2026-09-23 11:20 user: all shadow modes flipped to active; revert: set back to "shadow"
default_tier = "opus" # planner_router.load_cfg: candidate tier used for ordinary Planner decisions.
escalation_tier = "fable" # planner_router.load_cfg: premium tier reserved for hard or escalated decisions.
hard_complexity_min = 9 # planner_router.load_cfg: complexity at or above this value is a hard escalation.
hard_security = true # planner_router.load_cfg: security-sensitive work is a hard escalation.
hard_spec_review_request_changes_min = 2 # planner_router.load_cfg: repeated spec-review changes trigger hard escalation.

soft_threshold = 0.5 # planner_router.load_cfg: minimum soft escalation score.

# Review policy. Measurement 2026-09-18: every fallback-executed task got two reviews (daemon's sonnet one plus
# a hand-added opus one) and spec reviews ran on opus at 1.26 USD each -- reviews were costing as much as
# execution. complexity 1-3: hooks only, no review (CLAUDE.md step 7, unchanged). 4-6: exactly one review, on
# whichever model did not execute the task. 7-10: two reviews -- both reviews may run on the same account; the
# model differs from the executor. Spec review (before an executor ever sees the spec) only fires at
# complexity >= spec_review_min, and always runs on spec_review_tier. direct_merge_max/two_reviews_from/the
# complexity split above apply only when code_review = "always" below.
#
# User decision 2026-09-19: code reviews cost 44-45% of the last two goals and the human reviews every merged
# PR anyway, so code review is dropped except when the merged diff touches a security-sensitive path -- spec
# review (above) is unchanged and still gates complexity >= spec_review_min before an executor ever sees the
# spec. code_review: "never" (no code review, ever) | "security_paths" (review only a diff matching one of the
# globs below, or one changed_paths() could not determine -- fails closed) | "always" (today's pre-2026-09-19
# D1 behaviour, complexity-driven, unchanged). A security-path (or diff-unavailable) review always gets exactly
# one reviewer, on security_review_tier, swapped to the other Claude tier when the executor was that tier.
[review]
complementary = false # when true, two-review tasks get role-specialised packets; default false keeps one prompt for both reviewers; measured with scorecard --reviews --by role before any default change
spec_review_min = 6
direct_merge_max = 3
two_reviews_from = 7
spec_review_tier = "sonnet"
code_review = "security_paths"   # never | security_paths | always
security_review_tier = "sonnet"
security_paths = [
    "orchestrator/*.py",
    ".claude/hooks/**", ".claude/settings.json", ".orchestrator/pool.toml", ".orchestrator/protected-paths.txt",
    ".orchestrator/prompts/**", "skills/**", ".claude/skills/**",
    ".mcp*.json", ".mcp.worker.json", "Dockerfile", "docker-compose*.yml", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock",
]
# Semantic triggers use the same security-tier checklist: paths cover high-impact configuration and interfaces;
# patterns inspect added diff lines for authorization, schema, export, and tool/CLI changes.
semantic_paths = [
    "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock", "Dockerfile*", "docker/**", "**/migrations/**",
    "orchestrator/serve.py", "orchestrator/mcp.py", "orchestrator/bus_mcp.py", "orchestrator/cli.py",
]
semantic_patterns = { authorization = "(?i)\\b(?:bearer|token|authenticate|authorize|permission)\\b", database = "(?i)\\b(?:ALTER TABLE|CREATE TABLE)\\b", exports = "^\\s*__all__\\s*=", mcp_or_cli = "@mcp\\.tool|add_parser\\(" }

# Held-task risk areas: paths match changed files, patterns match added diff lines.
# Missing diff evidence sets all four areas true (fail closed).
[review.areas.auth]
paths = ["**/auth*", "auth*", "**/permissions*"]
patterns = ['(?i)\b(?:bearer|authenticate|authorize|permission)\b']
[review.areas.migrations]
paths = ["**/migrations/**", "migrations/**"]
patterns = ['(?i)\b(?:ALTER|CREATE|DROP) TABLE\b']
[review.areas.interfaces]
paths = ["**/api/**", "orchestrator/mcp.py", "orchestrator/cli.py"]
patterns = ['^\s*__all__\s*=', '@mcp\.tool|add_parser\(']
[review.areas.data_deletion]
paths = []
patterns = ['(?i)\b(?:DELETE FROM|TRUNCATE|DROP TABLE)\b', '\b(?:rmtree|unlink)\(']

+# Cache-aware disclosure
+
+## 1. Context routing shadow
+
+Every routed evidence item records its cacheability, effective cache-write cost, and cache-adjusted
+level. Cacheability is evaluated in order: worker-partial provenance is dynamic; test results are
+dynamic; source chunks pinned to the routing head are stable; everything else is semi. Effective
+cost is the presented text's character count divided by four, multiplied by one plus the provider's
+cache write ratio. Configured ratios override the telemetry defaults; a missing provider produces no
+cost.
+
+The only adjustment is `LONG` to `SHORT` when an item is dynamic, its effective cost exceeds
+`cache_downgrade_tokens` (default 600), and its routing reason is the generic fallback `ambiguous`.
+All named-rule reasons are exempt: `in_scope_file`, `security_path`, `failing_output`, `acceptance`,
+`skill_required_context`, `read_scope`, `section_items`, `prior_worker_overlap`, `unrelated`,
+`unrelated_memory`, `stale`, and `dependency`. `HIDE` never changes. Shadow mode records the proposed
+level without changing presented context. Active cache mode changes presentation only while the
+effective context-router mode is also active.
+
+Reproduce the aggregate with:
+
+    orchestrator scorecard --context --cache-shadow
+
+It reports the number and date range of `context_selection` rows and the share of evidence items whose
+cache-adjusted level differs from their presented level. With no matching rows it prints
+`no context_selection rows`.

Create orchestrator/steering_policy.py. evaluate(task, *, tasks, registry_doc, stale_evidence, gate_history, cfg) -> {"action": "continue"|"steer"|"cancel", "trigger": name|None, "reasons": [...], "message": text|None}. Triggers, deterministic, in this order: security_concern (a merged sibling changed a security path the task reads: from stale_evidence stale_paths matching [review] security_paths); dependency_changed (stale_evidence risk medium or high on the task's read scope); stuck (no registry event for [steering].stuck_after_s, default 900, while status running); out_of_scope (registry tool events touching paths outside write_scope and read_scope more than [steering].out_of_scope_events, default 3); repeated_failure (two gate reds with the same failure signature on this lineage). Action: steer for dependency_changed, out_of_scope, repeated_failure; cancel for security_concern when the task is not on the critical path, else steer; continue otherwise. The message names the trigger, lists the changed paths or the repeated failure, and never restates the spec. daemon tick: for every running execute task compute evaluate and record decision_log rows kind steering (add to KINDS) with candidates continue/steer/cancel, hard constraints, deterministic evidence, selected, mode; [steering].mode = "shadow" (dated comment; off|shadow|active). Active: call worker_control.steer or cancel with the message; shadow: rows only; never more than one steering per task per [steering].min_interval_s (default 1800). promotion FEATURES entry steering_policy with criteria: at least 20 shadow rows with a steer or cancel candidate and, once active, fewer fix rounds per task than the shadow baseline with no rise in token cost. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/12-steering-policy.md.
Spec review T-1262 folded in: (1) Inputs defined: gate_history = the list of daemon.failure_signature values of every gate-red round in the task's lineage (the fix_round_for chain up to the root), repeated_failure fires when the last two are equal; out_of_scope uses the worktree's `git status --porcelain` paths (not registry tool payloads): a path is outside scope when it matches no write_scope or read_scope entry by fnmatch (glob entries) or path prefix (directory entries); the count threshold applies to distinct paths. (2) evaluate(task, *, tasks, registry_doc, stale_evidence, gate_history, cfg, critical, now): critical is computed by the daemon as 'task is first in critical_path.rank over running plus ready tasks'; cancel is chosen only when critical is False AND the worktree has no commits beyond its base; any exception or missing input inside evaluate yields continue (fail closed) with reason evaluation_error. (3) daemon.tick wraps worker_control.steer/cancel in try/except: a failure writes a steering row with outcome error and does not consume the interval. (4) Interval and dedupe from persisted state: the last steering decision_log row for the task (bounded read of the last 500 rows) defines min_interval_s; a shadow row is written only when (trigger, evidence hash) differs from the task's last row, so ticks do not flood rows. (5) [steering] section is new: defaults live in code (mode shadow, stuck_after_s 900, out_of_scope_events 3, min_interval_s 1800); steering_policy.mode(cfg) validates and falls back to off on unknown values with invalid_config on the row; tests/test_pool.py gets a validation case (scope). (6) decision_log: steering rows carry trigger, severity, critical, action, evidence_hash, message_chars (never the message text) and the standard candidates/hard_constraints[REDACTED] fields; tests/test_decision_log.py (scope) updates any KINDS count assertions. (7) promotion.collect gains a steering_policy branch: n, steer and cancel counts, mean fix rounds of steered versus non-steered tasks over the window (from constraints.fix_round_for on the bus). (8) security_paths empty in [review] means fail closed: every orchestrator/*.py counts as a security path, mirroring the daemon. (9) Tests: shadow asserts steer and cancel are never called (unittest.mock); active calls once and respects min_interval_s; the error path writes an error row.
Spec review T-1268 folded in (final, overrides earlier wording): (1) Final signature: evaluate(task, *, tasks, registry_doc, stale_evidence, gate_history, cfg, critical, now) -> dict; the daemon and the tests use exactly this. (2) gate_history = [t['constraints']['failure_signature'] for every task in the fix_round_for chain (root included) whose pipeline.gate_reds > 0], newest last; failures.failure_signature is never recomputed. (3) out_of_scope: one `git status --porcelain -z` per running task per tick with a 5 s timeout (timeout, missing worktree or non-zero exit -> the trigger is skipped with reason git_unavailable); rename entries take the new path; paths under __pycache__, *.pyc, .orchestrator/, .venv/, node_modules/ and the worktree's .git are ignored. The no-commits guard is `git rev-list --count <merge-base with goal/<parent>>..HEAD` == 0 with the same timeout rule. (4) stale_evidence is the dict stale.evidence() returns on this branch (keys stale_paths, risk, risk_reasons, signals, moved_count, graph); cite it in the docstring and build fixtures from that shape; a missing key yields continue with reason missing_input. (5) Interval and dedupe: the interval clock counts only steering rows with mode active and outcome not error; shadow rows never start it; dedupe on (trigger, evidence_hash) applies only while the interval is running; after it expires a new row (and in active mode a new steer) is allowed even with unchanged evidence. (6) Active safety: skip tasks whose registry status is steering or cancelling, or whose pipeline.steer_epoch is newer than the registry epoch (steer in flight); a worker that exits between evaluate and the action is caught and logged as outcome worker_gone; critical uses the same critical_path.rank input the scheduler's wave order uses (pass the daemon's ranked list in). Cancel is SHADOW-ONLY in this task: in active mode the policy may steer but never cancels (a cancel candidate is logged and downgraded to steer), until a later promotion decision enables it. (7) decision_log gains a validator for kind steering (required keys: trigger, severity, critical, action, evidence_hash, message_chars plus the standard fields; a key named message is rejected); the omission test asserts message_chars is present and the message string is absent from the serialized row; every KINDS count assertion in the suite is updated.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.

import _harness
"""Account pool selection (PoolSel), the [[executors]] routing table (Executors), and Planner-transcript token
tallying (PlannerTally): bands, quota groups, cooldowns, budgets, scored ranking."""
import io, json, os, shutil, sys, tempfile, time, tomllib, unittest
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))  # `python -m unittest tests/test_pool.py` doesn't add this dir itself
from _harness import REPO, TMP  # noqa: F401
from orchestrator import planner_router, pool as P, spawn


def _iso(ts):
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"


def _assistant(ts, input_tokens=[REDACTED] output_tokens=[REDACTED] cache_read_input_tokens=[REDACTED]
    return json.dumps({"type": "assistant", "timestamp": ts, "message": {"usage": {
        "input_tokens": input_tokens, "output_tokens": output_tokens,
        "cache_read_input_tokens": cache_read_input_tokens}}}) + "\n"


def _user(ts):
    return json.dumps({"type": "user", "timestamp": ts, "message": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 999}}}) + "\n"


class PoolSel(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        P.PERSIST.unlink(missing_ok=True); P.PLANNER_USAGE.unlink(missing_ok=True); self.p = P.Pool()

    def test_affinity_reserve_cooldown_budget(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.p.pick("review").id, "A")            # both have review affinity, ties break to A
        A, B = self.p.get("A"), self.p.get("B")
        A.window_tokens=[REDACTED] * 0.7); self.p.save()       # above 1-reserve(0.35)=0.65 -> scouts go to B;
                                                                      # day_tokens left at 0 so A's daily budget (below
                                                                      # the reserve ceiling at this cap) doesn't also exclude it
        self.assertEqual(self.p.pick("scout").id, "B")
        self.assertEqual(self.p.pick("planner").id, "A")            # planner ceiling is 1.0
        self.p.cooldown(B, 600); self.assertIsNone(self.p.pick("review"))  # held, not failed
        self.p.resume("B"); self.assertEqual(self.p.pick("review").id, "B")
        B.day_tokens=[REDACTED] self.assertIsNone(self.p.pick("review"))
        self.assertEqual(P.Pool().get("A").window_tokens, A.window_tokens)  # persisted across restarts

    def test_pick_review_avoids_executing_account(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.p.pick("review", avoid="B").id, "A")   # B executed it; A has headroom
        self.assertEqual(self.p.pick("review", avoid="A").id, "B")
        self.p.cooldown(self.p.get("A"), 600)
        self.assertEqual(self.p.pick("review", avoid="B").id, "B")   # only B has headroom -> avoid is ignored

    def test_rate_limit_parsing_and_fallback(self):
        self.assertTrue(P.is_rate_limited("Error: You've hit your usage limit. Resets in 2h 15m"))
        self.assertEqual(P.parse_reset_hint("resets in 2h 15m"), 8100)
        self.assertEqual(P.parse_reset_hint("try again in 30 minutes"), 1800)
        self.assertEqual(P.parse_reset_hint("retry-after: 900"), 900)
        self.assertEqual(P.parse_reset_hint("nothing useful", default=42), 42)
        far = P.parse_reset_hint("You've hit your usage limit. Visit https://x to purchase more credits or try again at Sep 19th, 2099 2:00 PM.")
        self.assertGreater(far, 365 * 24 * 3600)                     # absolute date parsed, not the 1800 default
        self.assertEqual(P.parse_reset_hint("try again at Sep 19th, 2000 2:00 PM"), 60)  # past -> floor
        self.assertEqual([P.fallback_tier(c) for c in (3, 7, 9)], ["sonnet", "opus", None])
        self.assertTrue(P.is_rate_limited("You're out of usage credits. Switch to another model"))
        self.assertFalse(P.is_rate_limited("all good"))

    def test_trust_workspace(self):
        cfg = TMP / "prof"; spawn.trust_workspace(str(cfg), TMP / "wt" / "T-0099")
        self.assertTrue(json.loads((cfg / ".claude.json").read_text())["projects"][str(TMP / "wt" / "T-0099")]["hasTrustDialogAccepted"])

    def test_pool_toml_documents_roadmap_defaults(self):
        cfg = tomllib.loads((REPO / ".orchestrator" / "pool.toml").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(cfg["scheduler"]["mode"], "shadow")
        self.assertEqual(cfg["scheduler"], {
            **cfg["scheduler"],
            "duration_mode": "empirical",
            "duration_min_samples": 5,
            "duration_trim": 0.1,
            "reserve_imminent": True,
            "concurrency_mode": "adaptive",
            "merge_pressure_mode": "observe",
            "merge_queue_elevated": 3,
            "merge_queue_saturated": 5,
            "merge_conflicts_saturated": 2,
            "jev_mode": "shadow",
            "jev_max_pairs": 8,
            "jev_cache_ttl_s": 3600,
            "jev_cache_max_entries": 200,
        })
        self.assertEqual(cfg["jev"]["routing"]["mode"], "shadow")
        self.assertEqual(cfg["jev"]["routing"], {
            **cfg["jev"]["routing"], "max_adjustment": 0.25, "evidence_floor_n": 10,
        })
        self.assertEqual(cfg["jev"]["points"], {
            "scout_necessity": "shadow", "context_escalation": "shadow",
            "review_escalation": "shadow", "planner_relaunch": "shadow",
        })
        self.assertEqual(cfg["allocation"], {
            "mode": "shadow", "min_samples": 5, "latency_weight_usd_per_hour": 2.0,
            "critical_factor": 1.0, "non_critical_factor": 0.25,
        })
        self.assertEqual(cfg["strategy"], {"mode": "shadow", "min_samples": 10})
        self.assertEqual(cfg["speculation"], {
            "mode": "off", "min_fix_round_p": 0.5, "min_samples": 5, "min_retry_cost_usd": 1.0,
        })
        self.assertEqual(cfg["promotion"], {"min_samples": 20})

    def test_daemon_respawn_max_documented(self):
        cfg = tomllib.loads((REPO / ".orchestrator" / "pool.toml").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(cfg["daemon"]["respawn_max"], 3)
        daemon_lines = (REPO / ".orchestrator" / "pool.toml").read_text().splitlines()
        respawn_after = next(i for i, line in enumerate(daemon_lines) if line.startswith("respawn_after_s"))
        respawn_max = next(i for i, line in enumerate(daemon_lines) if line.startswith("respawn_max"))
        self.assertEqual(respawn_max, respawn_after + 1)

    def test_planner_routing_table_documented_defaults(self):
        cfg = tomllib.loads((REPO / ".orchestrator" / "pool.toml").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(cfg["planner"]["routing"], planner_router._DEFAULTS)
        self.assertEqual(cfg["limits"]["max_budget_usd"]["planner_shadow"], 1.5)
        with mock.patch.object(planner_router.notify, "notify") as notify:
            self.assertEqual(planner_router.load_cfg(cfg), planner_router._DEFAULTS)
            notify.assert_not_called()


class Reservations(unittest.TestCase):
    """Each run gets an isolated bus and ledger, including across fresh Pool instances."""

    def setUp(self):
        directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="orch-reservations-")
        self.addCleanup(directory.cleanup)
        self.sandbox = Path(directory.name)
        for module, name, value in (
            (P.bus, "STATE", self.sandbox),
            (P.bus, "TASKS", self.sandbox / "tasks"),

            (P, "PERSIST", self.sandbox / "pool_state.json"),
            (P, "PLANNER_USAGE", self.sandbox / "planner_usage.json"),
        ):
            patcher = mock.patch.object(module, name, value)

        self.cfg["limits"]["max_budget_usd"]["scout"] = 0.6

        self.p = P.Pool(self.cfg)

    def task(self):
        return P.bus.create_task("reservation", "spec", ["works"], ["x.py"],
                                 role="scout", parent="G-budget")

    def test_parallel_reservations_cannot_exceed_daily_budget(self):
        # Both callers loaded their pool before either claimed its share of the budget.
        other = P.Pool(self.cfg)
        first, second = self.task(), self.task()
        reservation = self.p.reserve("run-1", "A", "scout", first)
        self.assertIsNotNone(reservation)
        self.assertEqual(reservation["est_tokens"], 60)
        self.assertIsNone(other.reserve("run-2", "A", "scout", second))
        self.assertEqual(set(P.Pool(self.cfg).live_reservations()), {"run-1"})

    def test_estimate_never_zero_without_history(self):
        self.cfg["claude_accounts"][0].pop("usd_per_token")
        self.cfg["limits"]["default_tokens_per_usd"] = 250000
        tokens, usd = P.Pool(self.cfg)._reservation_estimate("A", "scout")
        self.assertEqual(usd, 0.6)
        self.assertEqual(tokens, 150000)

    def test_estimate_uses_token_derived_usd_for_codex_rows(self):
        self.cfg["limits"]["default_tokens_per_usd"] = 250000

        self.cfg["executors"] = [{"id": "codex-test", "provider": "codex",
                                  "model": "test", "roles": ["execute"]}]
        usage = {"input_tokens": 20000, "output_tokens": 5000}
        for i in range(5):
            task = P.bus.create_task(f"completed execute {i}", "spec", ["works"], ["x.py"],
                                     role="execute", parent="G-history")

        pool = P.Pool(self.cfg)
        tokens, usd = pool._reservation_estimate("codex-test", "execute")
        self.assertEqual(tokens, 25000)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(usd, 0.1)
        tasks = [P.bus.create_task(f"new execute {i}", "spec", ["works"], ["x.py"],
                                   role="execute", parent="G-budget") for i in range(3)]
        first = pool.reserve("run-1", "codex-test", "execute", tasks[0])
        self.assertIsNotNone(first)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(first["est_usd"], usd)
        self.assertEqual(P.Pool(self.cfg).live_reservations()["run-1"]["est_usd_source"], "tokens")
        pool.release("run-1", dict(usage))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(pool.reservation_history()["goals"]["G-budget"]["execute"]["usd"], usd)
        self.assertIsNotNone(pool.reserve("run-2", "codex-test", "execute", tasks[1]))
        self.assertIsNone(P.Pool(self.cfg).reserve("run-3", "codex-test", "execute", tasks[2]))
        self.assertEqual(set(pool.live_reservations()), {"run-2"})

    def test_expired_lease_with_live_pid_still_counts(self):
        first, second = self.task(), self.task()
        self.p.reserve("run-1", "A", "scout", first)
        P.bus.update(first["id"], status="running", pid=os.getpid())
        expiry = self.p.live_reservations()["run-1"]["lease_until"]
        with mock.patch.object(P.time, "time", return_value=expiry + 1):
            self.assertEqual(self.p.sweep_reservations(), [])
            self.assertIsNone(self.p.reserve("run-2", "A", "scout", second))

            P.bus.update(second["id"], status="running", pid=os.getpid())
